intro.title: Utility Types
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that uses TypeScript utility types to manage and transform user data. You will learn how utility types like Partial, Readonly, and Pick help you create flexible and type-safe code by modifying existing types. The main technologies involved are Angular components and TypeScript's built-in utility types. By the end, you'll understand how to apply these types to make your Angular applications more robust and maintainable.
intro.usecase: Utility Types are essential for managing complex data in real-world Angular applications, such as admin dashboards where user data must be selectively displayed or updated. For instance, when building a user profile form, developers can use `Partial<T>` to allow incremental updates without requiring all fields, or `Pick<T>` to extract specific properties for a summary panel. In interactive UI components like data tables with filters, `Omit<T>` helps create safe payloads by excluding internal IDs before sending data to an API. Mastering these types ensures type safety, reduces runtime errors, and streamlines development in scenarios like dynamic forms, API integrations, and state management.
